review.verdict: Clean riso-duotone linework and no cast violations, but the two essential story beats — the crane swapping the old sign for the new one, and the unmoved protesters — are missing entirely, so the right half reads as 'datacenter, new label' rather than 'renamed instead of fixed'; the hiker side also drops the fog/cliff stakes, leaving the joke to lean on text alone.</verdict>
revisionNotes: Add the protesters outside the datacenter (small cluster with backlash signs, unmoved) from the brief — it's missing entirely and is the beat that sells 'renamed, not fixed'.
Show a crane lowering the NEW NAME tag over a visible old sign being removed, not just a tag floating above the roof — without the swap, the right half reads as plain signage, not a joke.
Add a hint of fog and a cliff edge near the wrong-way bubble on the hiker's side so the danger of following the chatbot off-trail is visible, not just implied by the text.

Tighten the split: background currently reads as one uniform cream/blue field with a big empty gap center-top; add a clear vertical divider or distinct color block per half and scale both groups to ~1.1 to close the gap.
Nudge trail-sign from x=0.34 to about x=0.3, y=0.86 so it sits clear of the hiker's pointing arm/hand instead of crowding it.
Consider giving the datacenter a visible 'old sign' remnant (crossed-out or faded) beside the new one for a before/after read at a glance.

review.verdict: The split-scene concept is coherent and kind, but an oversized fog cloud swallows the divider and overwhelms both halves, the speech bubble erases the hiker's face, and a stray crossed-out sign and near-invisible cliff hurt clarity and polish enough to miss the bar.
revisionNotes: The 'wrongway-bubble' sits directly over the hiker's head, erasing the face entirely — scale it down to ~0.85 and shift it up-left so the head clears the bubble.

The 'fog' cloud is scaled far too large and straddles the divider, dominating both halves instead of staying in the hiker's path — scale it to ~0.6 and anchor it at x~0.32 so it stays on the left side only.
The cliff-edge prop reads as a tiny zigzag at ground level, not a dangerous drop — scale it up to ~1.0 and raise its silhouette so the hazard the hiker is walking into is unmistakable.

The crossed-out 'old-sign' floats ambiguously near the cloud with no clear anchor — pull it tighter against the datacenter/new-name-sign (attachTo datacenter, side top-left) so it reads as 'the sign being replaced,' not stray debris.
Pull the 'datacenter' anchor left (x~0.78) or drop scale to ~1.0 so it sits fully inside the safe area instead of bleeding off the right edge per the lint warning.
Protester placards are blank and small (scale 0.45) — bump scale to ~0.55 and add a simple raw-shape mark (fist or exclamation) so the 'still protesting' beat reads without needing a closer look.

review.verdict: The cast and concept mapping are right (humans for people, no robot miscasting), but a floating disconnected 'old sign' shape, an illegible cliff fragment, and a wrongway bubble adrift far from the hiker leave the composition cluttered and the left-side joke muddled — this needs a composition and polish pass before it's ready to publish.
revisionNotes: The old-sign (crossed rectangle meant to sit beside the datacenter) renders as an orphaned gray shape floating mid-frame near an unexplained '!' — anchor it tight to the crane/datacenter so it reads as the sign being swapped, not stray debris between the two halves.

The cliff-edge raw shape reads as an abstract jagged fragment, not a drop-off; simplify into a clear ledge silhouette and place it right at the hiker's lead foot so the danger is legible in 3 seconds.
The wrongway-bubble floats far above the hiker near the fog cloud with a weak tail — pull it in close to the hiker's head/pointing arm so it reads as what the hiker is following.

Each half carries 5-6 elements against the briefed 2-3 (left: hiker, trail sign, bubble, fog, cliff, stray old-sign; right: datacenter, crane, tag, old-sign, 2 protesters) — cut or merge shapes so the split scene reads as two clean groups.
Crane linework is thin and nearly disappears against the cream ground compared to the bold outlines on the hiker and building — thicken it to match the scene's line weight.

Add a clearer divider (gutter, ground line, or color break) between the hiker half and the datacenter half so the 'split scene' composition reads as intentional rather than a scatter of floating parts.
